findings.requirement_trace: ADR-0023 Stages/apply paragraph; Authorization and confinement
findings.root_cause: PendingCreate::execute runs bd create --graph on a request-owned snapshot and only then publishes the plan to <rendered_formula>.graph.json; a publish error discards the successful apply and is mapped to RenderFailed.
findings.recommended_fix: Check/publish the plan path before invoking bd create --graph (or report the committed ids with a publish-failure code).

findings.expected_oracle: render.md 'Appending JSON records' step 3: 'writes it as one compact UTF-8 line (embedded newlines stay escaped) followed by \n'.
findings.observed_result: Exit 0; nl.jsonl holds 2 physical lines '{"a":[1,' and '2]}', neither valid JSON. Nested whitespace is kept ({"z":[1, 2]}); only the top level is compacted. The concurrent-append family did not hit this because its records keep nested values on one line.
findings.root_cause: append_json_record re-serializes a BTreeMap<String, Box<RawValue>>, so each top-level value's raw text (including newlines and spaces) is written verbatim.
findings.recommended_fix: Re-serialize nested values compactly while preserving number lexemes (e.g. serde_json arbitrary_precision Value), or minify RawValue text outside strings.

concurrent_append_summary.oracle: Same matrix as run 2 (lib/r7append.py, seeds 7023/48611): one OS process per writer; each record is a separate sc-compose render --append invocation. Each line is parsed and compared field by field with its expected object (the pad holds quotes, backslashes, tabs, newlines, e-acute and check-mark; nested u is 'line\r\nx'). A torn line is any line that is not valid JSON or differs from its expected record. record_bytes is the measured mean line length. All 20 trials passed: 0 torn, 0 lost, 0 duplicates. Caveat: every record template keeps nested values on one line. A nested object or array that spans lines is written as a multi-line record even with a single writer (differential-n02); concurrency does not change that.
